q: Which statement about petroleum is correct?
options: It is a single compound of carbon and hydrogen.
It is a mixture of carbon and hydrogen elements.
It is a mixture of hydrocarbons.
It is a mixture of alcohols and carboxylic acids.
explain: Petroleum is a mixture of many different hydrocarbons, which are separated into fractions.

q: What are the products of the complete combustion of ethanol?
explain: Ethanol burns in excess oxygen: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O.

q: Which equation represents the reaction of ethanoic acid with sodium hydroxide?
explain: A base and an acid give a salt and water. The equation CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O is balanced.

q: Which monomer can form an addition polymer?
explain: Addition polymerisation needs a monomer with a C=C double bond. Propene has one but propane does not.

q: What is observed when ethene is bubbled through aqueous bromine?
explain: Ethene is unsaturated and reacts with bromine by addition, so the colour of the aqueous bromine disappears.

q: What is the role of ultraviolet light in the reaction of methane with chlorine?
options: It removes the hydrogen chloride formed.
explain: The reaction is photochemical: ultraviolet light provides the activation energy, Ea, needed to start the reaction.

q: Which row correctly describes the formation of poly(ethene)?
explain: Ethene molecules join by addition polymerisation, so the polymer is the only product.

q: Which pair of compounds are structural isomers of each other?
explain: Structural isomers have the same molecular formula (here C₄H₁₀O) but different structural formulae. The other pairs have different molecular formulae.

q: What is the name of the compound CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH?
explain: The chain has four carbon atoms, including the carbon in –COOH, and the –COOH group, so the name is butanoic acid.

q: The fractions in petroleum are separated by fractional distillation. Which property allows this separation?
options: The fractions have different solubilities in water.
The fractions have different electrical conductivities.
The fractions have different boiling points.
explain: Hydrocarbons of different chain length have different boiling points, so they condense at different heights in the fractionating column.

q: What is true of every addition reaction?
options: A small molecule is always lost.
explain: In an addition reaction two reactants join to give a single product.

q: Which two uses of ethanol are correct?
options: a fuel and a feedstock for making bitumen
explain: Ethanol is used as a solvent, for example in perfumes and paints, and as a fuel.

q: What is the formula of calcium ethanoate?
explain: Calcium forms Ca²⁺ and ethanoate is CH₃COO⁻, so two ethanoate ions are needed: (CH₃COO)₂Ca.

q: What is the repeat unit of poly(propene)?
explain: Propene, CH₃CH=CH₂, opens its double bond to give –CH₂–CH(CH₃)–, with the CH₃ group as a side group.

q: Methane reacts with chlorine in sunlight. Which pair of products forms in a monosubstitution?
explain: One H atom is replaced by one Cl atom: CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl.

q: Which statement about the members of a homologous series is correct?
options: Each member has the same relative molecular mass.
Each member has identical physical properties.
Each member has the same number of carbon atoms.
Each member differs from the next by a –CH₂– unit.
explain: Successive members differ by –CH₂–, so their relative molecular masses and physical properties change gradually along the series.

q: What is the name of the compound with the structural formula CH₃CH(OH)CH₃?
explain: It has three carbons with the –OH group on the second carbon atom, so it is propan-2-ol.

q: Which row correctly compares a fraction collected at the top of the fractionating column with a fraction collected at the bottom?
options: shorter chains | higher boiling point | less viscous
longer chains | lower boiling point | more viscous
shorter chains | lower boiling point | more viscous
shorter chains | lower boiling point | less viscous
explain: Fractions at the top have shorter hydrocarbon chains, lower boiling points, higher volatility and lower viscosity.

q: The repeat unit of poly(chloroethene) is –CH₂–CHCl–. What is the monomer?
explain: For an addition polymer, replace the single bond in the chain by a double bond: CH₂=CHCl is chloroethene.

q: What is the product when ethene reacts with hydrogen in the presence of a nickel catalyst?
explain: Hydrogen adds across the C=C bond: CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ → CH₃CH₃.

q: What is an advantage of making ethanol by hydration of ethene instead of by fermentation?
options: It uses a renewable raw material.
It works at a lower temperature.
It is faster and gives purer ethanol.
explain: Hydration is a fast continuous process that gives pure ethanol. Fermentation is slow, uses lower temperature and gives an impure product.

q: Ethanol is oxidised by warming it with acidified aqueous potassium manganate(VII). What colour change is seen?
explain: Acidified manganate(VII) is purple and is reduced to a colourless solution as it oxidises the ethanol to ethanoic acid.

q: What small molecule is lost when nylon forms from a dicarboxylic acid and a diamine?
explain: Nylon forms by condensation polymerisation: each amide link is formed with the loss of one molecule of water.

q: Which equation represents the monosubstitution of ethane by chlorine in ultraviolet light?
explain: In monosubstitution one hydrogen atom is replaced by one chlorine atom, and the displaced hydrogen forms HCl. The other equations are not balanced or show other products.

q: What is the formula of the carboxylic acid with four carbon atoms in each molecule, using the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH?
explain: The –COOH group contains one carbon atom, so the four-carbon acid has n = 3, giving C₃H₇COOH.

q: What is the name of CH₃CH=CHCH₃?
explain: The chain has four carbons and the double bond starts at carbon 2, giving but-2-ene.

q: Which fraction from petroleum is used to make roads?
explain: Bitumen is the thick residue at the bottom of the column and is used for road surfaces.

q: Which structural formula represents the product of the reaction of ethene with bromine?
explain: Bromine adds across the double bond, so each carbon atom gets one bromine atom. The product is 1,2-dibromoethane.

q: Which link joins the monomer units in nylon?
explain: Nylon is a polyamide, so its monomer units are joined by amide links, –CONH–.

q: What is a disadvantage of making ethanol by hydration of ethene?
options: It produces a mixture of ethanol and carbon dioxide.
It needs yeast, which dies easily.
The ethene comes from petroleum, which is non-renewable.
explain: Ethene is made from petroleum, a finite resource. Fermentation uses sugar from plants, which is renewable.
